restorePurchaseIntro: Already linked your purchase? Sign in with that email to restore Pro.

restorePurchaseWebStep: Then sign in on this website with the same email to restore Pro. No new purchase is needed.
restorePurchaseHelp: If the app does not recognize your purchase, use Restore purchase with the original Apple ID first. The app must support Email account. If already linked, use the original email.
proCopy: One purchase unlocks price alerts, offline alerts and cross-device data sync.
proSyncNote: Link your Pro purchase to an email, then sign in with the same email on Web and in apps to sync monitors, public addresses, contacts, alerts and preferences.
syncRequiresPro: Data sync requires Pro. A free account keeps your data on this device only.

poolsNote: Compare public PRL pools, without an address.
calculatorNote: Output, operating cost and break-even price.
comparisonExplanation: PRL per PH·day: observed blocks × reward ÷ hashrate, normalized to one day, minus the pool fee.
poolWeekLuckExplanation: Estimated yield = today's theoretical yield × the pool's 7-day block luck (blocks found ÷ blocks its hashrate should have found, sampled every 5 minutes) × (1 − pool fee); PRL/PH·day; green = highest.
poolWeekLuckFallback: Pools without “7d” have less than a week of samples: blocks actually found × block reward ÷ hashrate.
ppsExplanation: PPS uses network expected output minus the pool's Real Cost (its fee until Real Cost is measured). SOLO is a lottery. Neither is ranked as the best measured yield.
sampleExplanation: Small samples contain fewer than 20 blocks and can fluctuate widely. The green Top measured label compares pools with enough samples from the same source.
heroExplanation: HeroMiners software fee is a 3% reference; edit the total fee to match your software.
mixedSources: Primary data uses a 24h window. Extra source rows use the last 1,000 network blocks from MiningPoolStats. Pool API indicates hashrate or fees supplemented or corrected using the pool’s own API.
referenceNote: GPU hashrate, power and purchase price are editable reference values from the App catalog, not live hardware quotes. Amounts are shown in USD, with a secondary currency when enabled and an exchange rate is available.
waitingNetwork: Waiting for price and network data. Enter scenario values to calculate offline.
costExplanation: Daily electricity + rent ÷ output after fees. Hardware cost is shown separately through payback.
calculationExplanation: Expected output uses live network difficulty and block reward. Hours scale output, electricity and rent together. Projections apply your monthly difficulty growth with price, reward and costs held fixed. Pool luck is not predicted.
poolYieldBasis: Daily PRL you keep for 1 PH/s, after the pool's cut.
poolOwnApiMissing: This pool's own API is not responding right now, so its figures come from other sources.
extensionIntro: Manage your PRL in the browser sidebar. Receive and send directly in the extension.
extensionDesktop: Requires desktop Chrome 120 or later. On mobile? Open this page on your computer to install.
extensionStoreRelease: Chrome Web Store · Updates automatically · 16 languages
extensionStoreStep: Add it from the Chrome Web Store
extensionStoreStepNote: Open the store page with the button above, add the extension to Chrome and confirm.
extensionMovedNote: The store version is a separate extension and starts with no wallets. Make sure every wallet’s recovery phrase is backed up, then restore each wallet in the store version and check its balance. After that, remove the manual build on chrome://extensions.
extensionManualNote: Only if you can’t use the Chrome Web Store. The ZIP installs as a separate extension from the store version and does not update itself.
extensionStep1Note: Download the ZIP above and extract it to a permanent folder. Keep that folder after installation.
extensionStep2Note: Copy the address below and open it in the Chrome address bar.
extensionStep3Note: Enable “Developer mode”, click “Load unpacked” and select the extracted folder containing manifest.json.
extensionStep4: Open and set up your wallet
extensionStep4Note: Pin Pearl Hub Wallet from Chrome’s extensions menu. Click its icon to open the sidebar, then create a wallet or restore with your recovery phrase.
extensionExistingNote: Click the Pearl Hub Wallet icon in the Chrome toolbar. Enter your recovery phrase only inside the extension, and follow the backup steps when creating a wallet.
pushSaveError: Notification settings were not synced. Reconnect and try again.
pushNeedsConnection: Offline alerts are not connected. Enable notifications on the Alerts page.
pushTimeout: Push service timed out. Check your connection and try again.
pushConnectError: Could not connect to the browser push service. Check your network and notification permissions.
pushPermission: Allow browser notifications and try again.
pushSetupMonitor: Enable browser notifications first; offline alerts for this monitor will then be enabled.
offlineGuide: After activating Pro and allowing notifications, enable Offline alerts for each monitor on the Workers page. Choose 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes. The server checks about every 3 minutes, alerts after the offline threshold, and notifies again after roughly 1 minute of stable recovery. Pool timeouts are not treated as outages. Workers already offline when enabled do not trigger alerts.
extensionUpdateNote: Back up every wallet’s recovery phrase first. Then replace the files in the original install folder with the new version and reload the extension on chrome://extensions. Your wallets are normally kept. If the wallet list is empty after reloading (early test builds used a different extension ID), restore each wallet with its recovery phrase.
f2Help: How to get the read-only page link
f2Step1: Sign in to f2pool.com, click your avatar (top right) → Account Settings.
f2Step2: Pick Read-Only Page in the sidebar, then click Generate.
f2Step3: Tick PRL under Coins; under Permissions tick both “mining hashrate and worker list” and “revenue data, including payment information”.
f2Step4: Generate, copy the link, and paste it above.
f2Permission: With the “without payment information” permission everything else still works, but Total Paid shows 0.
f2ReadOnly: The link is read-only — it cannot move funds — and you can revoke it on F2Pool at any time.

poolRealCostPeriodIntro: Real Cost estimates use the following measurement periods. PPLNS and PROP require at least 5 days of data within the last 7 days, the pool’s own per-block effort for that time, and enough pool hashrate to expect at least 100 blocks; otherwise “—” is shown.
poolRealCostPeriodMissing: No measurement period is available yet. PPLNS and PROP require at least 5 days of data within the last 7 days, the pool’s own per-block effort for that time, and enough pool hashrate to expect at least 100 blocks; otherwise “—” is shown.
poolRealCostPpsUpdate: PPS periods end at %@ each day and move forward once the pool has settled that day, usually a few hours later. Until then, the previous period is shown.
poolSchemeIntro: A pool's payout scheme decides how it pays you, and who carries the cost of block luck and orphaned blocks.
poolSchemePpsPay: Every valid share earns a fixed amount at the network's theoretical rate, however many blocks the pool finds.
poolSchemePpsRisk: Bad luck and orphans cost the pool, not your income.
poolSchemePpsIncome: The steadiest: the same hashrate earns about the same every day. The pool takes the risk, so its fee is usually higher.
poolSchemePpsVariants: PPS+ and FPPS are variants that pay the block reward per share the same way. PPS+ shares out transaction fees PPLNS-style; FPPS adds their average to each share. PRL blocks carry very little in fees, so the difference is mostly the pool fee.
poolSchemePropPay: Each block the pool finds is split by everyone's portion of the round: the shares submitted since the pool's previous block.
poolSchemePropRisk: A long round spreads one block's reward over more shares; an orphan pays nothing, and everyone in the round shares the loss.
poolSchemePropIncome: Moves with the pool's luck. Open to pool hopping: those who join early in a round and leave when it runs long dilute those who stay.
poolSchemePplnsPay: Each block is split by everyone's portion of the last N shares, which can span several rounds.
poolSchemePplnsRisk: As with PROP, bad luck and orphans reduce your pay.
poolSchemePplnsIncome: Moves with the pool's luck, but more smoothly than PROP. You reach full pay once your shares fill the window, and they keep earning for a while after you leave, so hopping gains nothing. Suits staying with one pool.
poolSchemeSoloPay: You get the whole block reward, less the pool fee, only when your own hashrate finds a block; otherwise nothing.
poolSchemeSoloRisk: If your block is orphaned, the work earns nothing.
poolSchemeSoloOdds: At today's difficulty, 1 PH/s finds a block about every %@ days on average.
poolSchemeOrphan: When two pools find a block at almost the same moment, the chain keeps only one; the other is orphaned and earns no reward. PPS pools absorb orphans themselves; on PROP, PPLNS and SOLO you do, so a low orphan rate matters there.
poolSchemeOrphanRate: The table's orphan rate = orphans ÷ blocks over the last 7 days (fewer while data builds up; the days are then shown). It comes from two sources: the pool's own block list, if it publishes each block's status, and the orphaned blocks the lordofpearls explorer's node saw, set against the blocks the chain credits to the pool. Neither catches every orphan, so each pool shows the higher of the two, labelled with its source. Pools whose blocks the explorer cannot attribute show “—”. Real Cost for PPLNS and PROP already includes the orphan loss.
poolSchemeChoose: For steady daily income, or if you switch pools often: a PPS scheme. If you will stay with one pool: PPLNS usually costs less and luck evens out over time, but check its Real Cost and orphan rate.
poolHistoryNotes: The chart shows hashrate over the last 7 days; unavailable data appears as “—”.
poolContractNotes: Real cost = (1 − earnings after pool fee ÷ theoretical earnings) × 100%; negative means earnings above theory. PPS, PPS+ and FPPS use dated settlement measurements. PPLNS and PROP use the pool’s blocks and published pool fee over the sample window with block luck taken out: the pool’s own per-block effort shows how much work its blocks took, so what remains is the fee and the work the pool loses. Pools that publish no per-block effort, such as PearlHash, show “—”, as do missing data and other schemes. Software and transfer fees are excluded. PF shows PPS and PPLNS separately. PPLNS and PROP require at least 5 days of data within the last 7 days, the pool’s own per-block effort for that time, and enough pool hashrate to expect at least 100 blocks; otherwise “—” is shown.
oneShotAlertNote: Turns off after triggering. You can turn it on again manually.
repeatingAlertNote: Stays on after triggering. Notifies again when the condition resets and is met again, with a cooldown between alerts.
appDownloadDescription: Track PRL prices, pools and your wallet on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
appScanDownload: Scan with your iPhone or iPad to download.
singleAddressNote: Only this address is counted. Other receiving and change addresses that the same wallet rotates to are not included.
klineUnavailable: Couldn't load SafeTrade candlesticks. Try again later.
klineHelp: Use the left and right arrow keys to inspect candles, and + or − to zoom.
txInvalid: Enter a transaction ID: 64 characters, 0–9 and a–f.
txNotFound: Transaction not found. One sent moments ago can take a little while to appear.
txTruncated: Only the first %@ are listed. Open the explorer for the full list.
txRateLimited: Too many lookups. Try again in a minute.
txBroadcastNote: Paste a transaction signed elsewhere. It is decoded here for you to check, and nothing is sent until you press Broadcast. A broadcast transaction can’t be called back.
txRawInvalid: This isn’t a signed transaction in hex. Check that it was copied in full.
txBroadcastDone: Broadcast. It is confirmed once it is in a block.
txBroadcastKnown: The network already has this transaction.
txSendRateLimited: Too many broadcasts. Try again in a minute.
txSendUnknown: No answer from the network, so it isn’t known whether the transaction went out. Look it up, or broadcast it again: sending the same transaction twice is safe.
txRebroadcastDone: Rebroadcast: the transaction went to the network again.
txRebroadcastConfirmed: This transaction is already in a block; there is nothing to rebroadcast.
txRebroadcastGone: Neither indexer has this transaction any more, so it can’t be rebroadcast from its ID. Broadcast its signed hex instead, e.g. from the wallet that sent it.
txIsTxid: This is a transaction ID, not a signed transaction. To rebroadcast a transaction the network has seen, look it up and choose Rebroadcast.
